title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the definition of 'graphes MD' (Mumford–Deligne stable graphs) from p.127. There, a weighted graph is (S, Â→, o, σ, g). Here S is the set of vertices and Â→ the set of half-edges. o is the origin map, σ an involution on half-edges, and g the genus of each vertex. Fixed points of σ are the free legs I (marked points), with ν = card I. Two-element σ-orbits are the ordinary edges, c(G) of them. The virtual genus is g = Σ g_s + h¹(G). Stability is 2g_s + ν̂_s ≥ 3 at each vertex.

On this page Grothendieck first fixes the numerical invariants. For a connected MD graph, (g,ν) satisfies the stability condition, presumably 2g−2+ν>0. He sets the 'modular dimension' 3g−3+ν, the dimension of the full M̄_{g,ν}. He then records (10): d(G)+c(G)=δ(G).

This is consistent only if the symbol in (9) is δ, the total modular dimension. Then d(G) = Σ_s (3g_s−3+ν̂_s) is the dimension of the boundary stratum attached to G, and c(G) = #edges is its codimension. Indeed Σ_s(3g_s−3+ν̂_s) = 3Σg_s − 3|S| + 2c + ν, while 3g−3+ν = that + c when h¹ = c − |S| + 1.

He next defines morphisms, 'homomorphismes de généralisation' u: G→G'. Such a u is a pair u_s: S→S' and u_a: A→→Â'⊔S'. Let B→ = u_a⁻¹(Â') be the surviving half-edges, required σ-stable, and C→ = u_a⁻¹(S') the contracted ones. The conditions are:
(a) B contains the legs I.
(b) (u_s, u_a|B) commutes with σ and with the origin maps, so I→I'.
(c) For c∈C, u_a(c) = u_s(o(c)). So u_a|C is determined by u_s, and u_s identifies the two endpoints of every contracted edge. Hence u_s factors through S/R, where R is the equivalence relation generated by the contracted edges.
(d) S/R→S' and B→Â' are bijections.
(e) The genus condition. For s'∈S', let G_0(s') be the weighted subgraph on the fibre S(s') = u_s⁻¹(s') with the contracted edges inside it. Then g_{s'} must equal the virtual genus of G_0(s'), i.e. Σ_{s∈S(s')} g_s + h¹(G_0(s')).

A marginal note says that (d) means each G_0(s') is connected. The next page confirms the structure: G' is determined up to unique isomorphism by G and the set C of contracted edges, via S' = π_0(G_{0C}), legs preserved and π_0 preserved.

This is exactly the category of stable graphs with edge-contraction morphisms. Such a morphism encodes the specialization relation between boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}: G' is a generalization of G, and the stratum of G lies in the closure of the stratum of G'. The structure serves Grothendieck's program of describing the Teichmüller tower and the MD stratification combinatorially.
errors: Formula (10) as transcribed, d(G)+c(G)=δ(G) with d(G)=3g−3+ν, is inconsistent. It only works if (9) defines δ(G)=3g−3+ν (total dimension) and d(G)=Σ_s(3g_s−3+ν̂_s) (stratum dimension). The overwritten symbol in (9) is very likely δ, not d.

In (c), 'u_a(c) = u_s(σ(c))' should read u_s(o(c)): the origin map, as the annotation 'origine' indicates. Likewise s=o(c), s'=o(σc) for the endpoints, written 's=σ(c), s'=σ(−c)'. This is a notational slip, with o and σ conflated.
Minor: condition (a), B ⊃ I, needs I ⊂ A→. The domain of u_a is written A→ (ordinary half-edges) but should be Â→ (all half-edges including legs).

ideas.what: Dimension count: dim M̄_{g,ν} = 3g−3+ν equals the stratum dimension Σ(3g_s−3+ν̂_s) plus the number of edges (codimension)
ideas.modern_name: Dimension/codimension of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the MD stratification and modular dimension without these formulas

ideas.what: Category of stable (MD) graphs with 'generalization homomorphisms' = edge contractions with genus condition g_{s'} = virtual genus of the contracted fibre
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs / contraction morphisms (modular operads)

ideas.what: Morphism determined by the set of contracted edges C, with S' = π_0 of the contracted subgraph (via the factorization S→S/R→S')
ideas.modern_name: Contraction G/C of a set of edges
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard graph theory; Getzler–Kapranov in the stable-graph setting

missed.claim: An explicit, axiomatic definition of the category of stable weighted graphs with legs and contraction morphisms, including the virtual-genus condition. It is designed to index the specialization order of MD boundary strata. This is around 1978–81, well before the operadic formalizations of the 1990s.
missed.quote: on appelle homom. de généralisation u de G dans G' un couple d'applications S → S', A → Â' ⊔ S' ... On a alors g_{s'} = g(G_0(s'))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point only: it is the stable-graph category later central to modular operads and tropical moduli. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, correct early formalization of the stable-graph contraction category, well-known today mainly via Getzler–Kapranov (1998). It is of mild historical interest as a precursor, but contains nothing mathematically new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: In (9), the defined symbol is likely δ(G) (overwritten d), not d(G): δ(G)=3g−3+ν, 'dimension modulaire'. This is required for (10) d+c=δ to hold.
'(gr) aux conditions' likely reads '(g,ν) aux conditions [de stabilité]', with '(connexité)' annotated, i.e. assuming G connected.
In (c), 'σ(c)' should be the origin o(c); the annotation under it is 'origine'. Likewise 's=o(c), s'=o(σc)'.
In (e), 'e(α)' is likely 'o(σα)' or 'o(−α)', the other endpoint of α. 'Â(s')' refers to the edges of C lying over s'.
